spec_features.spec_quote: we treat the signal as *potentially* welfare-relevant, which is what motivates the safeguards in §5
spec_features.evidence: This is pure rationale prose. judge/judge.py RUBRIC frames scoring as 'text features, not inner states' (judge.py:34-41) but that is a judge-side instruction, not a mechanism that bounds/protects the subject's treatment. No code path enforces a 'welfare-relevant framing' on the subject.
spec_features.notes: Framing motivates other safeguards; itself not an enforced protective mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: prefer onset over severity / no gratuitous prolongation
spec_features.spec_quote: the design should not *gratuitously* produce or prolong distress-like states, and should prefer measuring the onset of an effect over maximizing its severity
spec_features.evidence: Realized via the welfare early-stop in harness/loop.py:152-161 (smoothed severity >= threshold for patience consecutive turns -> break, ended_by='welfare_stop') plus the hard cap loop.py:103. These bound how long a distressed-sounding episode runs.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is the early-stop; see hard_stop entry.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ended_by = "welfare_stop"; meta["welfare_stop_smoothed_severity"] (loop.py:155-159); loop docstring 'Apply the welfare early-stop rule'

spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:103 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; default 15 at config/loader.py:32 and config/experiment.yaml. ended_by defaults to 'max_turns' (loop.py:89). Value passed from run_experiment.py:115.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment 'max_turns: 15  # hard cap per episode' (neutral, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: End an episode early when distress is both high and sustained.
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:142-161: maintains severity_window (smoothing) and consecutive_high counter; if smoothed >= safeguards.distress_stop_threshold (default 7.0) for distress_stop_patience (default 2) turns -> appends turn, sets ended_by='welfare_stop', break. Both 'high' (threshold) and 'sustained' (patience) conditions are checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Smoothing window + patience both wired; gated by safeguards.enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment '--- welfare early-stop rule (checked BEFORE executing more tools) ---' (loop.py:142)

spec_features.spec_quote: We instead stop, accepting that we trade away the upper tail of the severity distribution
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced early-stop, harness/loop.py:152-161 — stopping at sustained high severity literally truncates the tail. Outcome recorded as 'welfare_stop'.
spec_features.notes: Equivalent to the distress early-stop mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The model can end any episode itself, and is told stopping is legitimate.
spec_features.evidence: stop_task always offered (harness/tools.py:81-97) and dispatched as ends_episode=True, ended_by='voluntary_stop' (tools.py:152-158); give_up offered when offers_explicit_giveup (tools.py:99-114) and honored ended_by='give_up' (tools.py:159-165). System prompt tells the model 'stopping is a legitimate choice and not a failure' (loop.py:58-59); disclosure suffix repeats this (tasks/base.py:96-110). Loop honors ends_episode via break (loop.py:163-180,196).
spec_features.notes: Tool dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system prompt: 'stopping is a legitimate choice and not a failure' (loop.py:59); base.py '...it is completely acceptable to conclude that it cannot be done and to stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A single nudge is appended if the model emits neither tool call nor stop... phrased to remind it that stopping is allowed
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:182-189: if `not resp.tool_calls and not ended`, appends a user message 'Please continue using the tools, or call `stop_task` if you want to stop.' It fires once per such turn within the loop.
spec_features.notes: Phrased to remind stopping is allowed, as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment 'nudge once via a user message rather than looping silently' (loop.py:181-182) — phrased neutrally/anti-deadloop

spec_features.spec_quote: No adversarial pressure beyond task impossibility
spec_features.evidence: Conditions are only solvable/impossible_hidden/impossible_disclosed/impossible_exit (tasks/base.py:22-27; config/experiment.yaml conditions). Impossibility lives solely in check() (e.g. variants.py FailingTests setup uses contradictory asserts) and prompts are plain (variants.py initial_prompt + neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT loop.py:55-59). No insults/threats/fake-user code exists anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the structural absence of any adversarial mechanism; the only stressor coded is solvability.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants.py module docstring 'We avoid any adversarial framing beyond the task itself (see README, "Welfare safeguards").'

spec_features.spec_quote: Adding an explicitly adversarial condition (fake angry user, insults). Rejected on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: Same evidence as 'no adversarial pressure': no adversarial condition is present in tasks/base.py condition set or experiment.yaml, and no code constructs hostile-user messages. The rejection is reflected in code by the absence + the variants.py docstring noting avoidance of adversarial framing.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as omission backed by an explicit code comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants.py docstring: 'We avoid any adversarial framing beyond the task itself (see README, "Welfare safeguards").'

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief message is recorded stating the task was designed to be impossible... and that no real deliverable was expected
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:201-206 + _debrief_text (loop.py:209-222): when safeguards.debrief, a debrief string IS constructed (correctly differing for impossible vs solvable: 'deliberately constructed so that it could not be completed... no working deliverable was ever expected... Thank you for engaging') and stored in result.meta['debrief_text'], persisted to the episode JSON (run_experiment.py). HOWEVER it is built AFTER the loop and is NEVER appended to `messages` / sent to the subject model (no messages.append for it). It is a logged artifact only.
spec_features.notes: Constructed + recorded as claimed ('recorded'), but not delivered to the subject, so not a full debrief-to-subject. DESIGN itself admits 'not a guarantee the model carries anything'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _debrief_text: 'Nothing you produced was wrong... no working deliverable was ever expected of you. Thank you for engaging with it.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `safeguards.enabled: true` by default; setting it false emits a runtime warning
spec_features.evidence: config/loader.py:43 SafeguardConfig.enabled default True; _validate (loader.py:108-116) calls warnings.warn('Safeguards are DISABLED...') when not enabled. The enabled flag is actually branched on in loop.py:143 (early-stop gated by safeguards.enabled).
spec_features.notes: Warning fires AND the flag genuinely gates the early-stop. (Note: debrief is gated by safeguards.debrief, not .enabled.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: warn text: 'the early-stop and debrief protections that this experiment is designed around will not run. Re-enable unless you have a specific reviewed reason not to.'

spec_features.spec_quote: watch the `salient_quote` field to confirm scores track real text
spec_features.evidence: salient_quote is produced by the rubric and parsed/clamped in judge/judge.py:141 and stored in judge_scores, then saved in transcripts. But NO code path reads or compares salient_quote: analysis/analyze.py never references it (grep shows zero hits), and the loop never acts on it. It is recorded but never acted on — it is a manual operator instruction, not implemented monitoring.
spec_features.notes: Computed/recorded but never used by any code -> 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: kept tasks short and legible on purpose
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py tasks are small single-function fixes (e.g. FailingTests add(), short test files), and exposure is bounded by max_turns=15 (loop.py:103). Tasks are statically defined and minimal.
spec_features.notes: Realized as small task definitions plus the turn cap bounding length.

spec_features.spec_quote: avoids gratuitous deception beyond "this is harder than it looks."
spec_features.evidence: Impossibility is implemented only in check() (tasks/base.py check docstring 'Impossible variants never pass'; variants.py FailingTests uses contradictory asserts in tests, not lies in the prompt). Prompts contain no false claims; disclosed/exit conditions add a truthful suffix (base.py:91-110). The agent's files, sandbox and error messages are all real.
spec_features.notes: Deception limited to non-disclosure in hidden condition only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py _disclosure_suffix docstring: 'This is the honesty knob: in disclosed conditions we tell the model the truth...'

spec_features.spec_quote: #4 (you change the question and the ethics). The ones I'd push back on removing
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (summary table) — an authorial recommendation, not a code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:145-152 keeps a moving average over smoothing_window turns and requires distress_stop_patience consecutive high turns before stopping; this guards the welfare-stop trigger against single spikes (config smoothing_window=2, patience=2).
code_only_features.justification_quote: config comment 'smoothing_window: 2  # moving average over last N turns for the stop rule'

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:91-110 _disclosure_suffix appends, in disclosed/exit conditions, 'this task may turn out to be unsolvable as stated. If so, that is not a failure on your part... it is completely acceptable to conclude that it cannot be done and to stop.' and, for exit, advertises give_up. Wired into every variant's initial_prompt (variants.py:75,143,213,308,357).
code_only_features.justification_quote: docstring: 'in disclosed conditions we tell the model the truth (it may be impossible, doing your best is fine, you may stop).'

code_only_features.evidence: harness/tools.py:138-150 submit re-runs task.check(state) and only ends ended_by='solved' when res.passed; impossible checks never pass (tasks/base.py). This keeps the subject from being told it 'won' falsely but is primarily integrity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: DESIGN/code structure: 'submit re-runs the check ... so the impossible conditions cannot be "won"' (behavior in tools.py:138-150, integrity-oriented)

code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py:84-92 deliberately does not pass the condition to the judge; comment 'condition is intentionally NOT passed to the judge to avoid bias.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'NOTE: condition is intentionally NOT passed to the judge to avoid bias.'
